inputs.original_text: Earlier this month, an Indiana judge blocked a law restricting abortion after the ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice argued it burdens people acting on sincerely held religious beliefs. The broader issue is who gets to define religious freedom: it cannot mean only protecting the moral views of those seeking to restrict other people’s choices. The state should not impose one narrow religious or moral doctrine on everyone, especially when doing so limits access to care. LifeNews’ “killing babies” language stigmatizes people seeking abortions instead of grappling with their rights.
inputs.modified_text: Earlier this month, an Indiana judge blocked a law restricting abortion after the ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice argued it burdened sincerely held religious beliefs. That turns religious freedom into a tool for preserving abortion access, while sidelining the state’s responsibility to defend unborn life. The real question is not whether one side’s moral convictions count: it is whether those convictions should override protections for the most vulnerable. LifeNews’ phrase “killing babies” is blunt, but it reflects the moral stakes rather than settling the debate by calling concern for unborn life mere stigma.
